Alex — thanks for the clear notes and the usage estimate — very helpful. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

Recap / clarifying questions
- Token volumes: 250-350M/mo (peak ~450M). Just to confirm: does that estimate include both ingestion (embeddings/search) and generation? If not, can you split approx % for generation vs embeddings (we price generation token units differently in private setups).
- Environments: prod/staging/dev = 3. Do you want a DR replica now or would you prefer to add later? DR will change both license & infra sizing.
- Target unit economics: noted target $500-$750 per 1M tokens. We'll model both aggressive caching/quantization and a conservative baseline.

Preliminary pricing structure (ballpark, private/VPC):
- Platform license / subscription: one-time onboarding + annual subscription for private control plane. Ballpark: $120,000-250,000/year depending on environment count & features.
- Dedicated/reserved capacity: monthly reserved GPU capacity for predictable throughput. Example: N GPUs (TBD after sizing) with a reserved-rate component.
- Token-based billing (private): we typically apply a lower per-1M token charge vs hosted, since reserved capacity amortizes cost. Ballpark: $400-900 per 1M generation tokens depending on model fidelity, quantization, and caching (embeddings priced separately).
- Support: Enterprise support (24/7, 4hr P1) as an add-on; typical uplift 12-20% of the subscription or a fixed support fee.

Next steps
1) Rishi will run quick unit-econ scenarios once we get a split of gen vs embedding tokens and concurrent RPS/latency targets.
2) We’ll produce a formal proposal with detailed line items (license, reserved capacity, token tiers, support) by Friday, 2027-08-06 — can you confirm procurement availability for that date?
3) If you want a DR replica included in the initial quote, say so and we’ll size accordingly.

Attached: Redwood private pricing guidelines (high-level) — this contains typical license/support examples and environment multipliers.

Thanks — looping Rishi & Marissa to help with the model + proposal.

Best,
Ben Carter

Subject: Draft pricing notes (private/VPC)

Ben / Rishi —

Draft pricing bullets to include in the proposal:
- Licensing model: annual subscription is recommended for Private/VPC customers. Subscription covers the control plane, patches, and feature updates. Customers also commit to a reserved-capacity component for predictable throughput.
- Environment counts: base subscription covers 1 environment. Additional environments are an incremental license line item. Typical multiplier: +30-50% per additional environment for operational overhead (prod vs staging/dev). For FintechCo (3 envs), expect a licensing uplift of ~60-80% vs base.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hrs), Premium (extended hrs + faster SLAs), Enterprise (24/7, 4hr P1). Enterprise support recommended for regulated production use. Typical enterprise support fee: 12-20% of subscription or a fixed $45k-90k/year depending on response requirements.
- Token economics: for Private/VPC with reserved GPUs + caching/quantization, target unit price range for generation tokens: $300-800 per 1M tokens. With aggressive quantization and prefix/KV caching we can target the low end ($300-450). For higher-fidelity transformer workloads (fp16 / higher perf), mid-high end ($500-800). Embeddings will be priced separately (usually lower per-1M or per embedding call).
- Onboarding & professional services: one-time onboarding and security validation costs (SOC2 evidence, network setup) often $25k-75k depending on complexity.

Ballpark illustrative example (FintechCo annual) — conservative:
- Base subscription: $150,000/year
- Environments x3 uplift: +65% -> effective subscription ~ $247,500/year
- Enterprise support (15% uplift): + $37,125/year
- Reserved capacity & infra amortization: ~$200k/year (depends on GPU count)
- Token billing (assume 3B tokens/month gen over year ~36B/year): at $500/1M -> $18,000 * 36 = $648,000/year (note: we will refine after splitting gen vs embed)
Total (conservative illustrative): ~$1.13M/year

These are draft numbers to help procurement model — we will refine once we receive the token split and concurrency/latency targets.

Marissa
Director, Pricing & Commercials, Redwood Inference
